title: Series and convergence
summary: When an infinite series converges, and how fast. $\sum 1/n^s$ converges for real $s>1$ and diverges at $s=1$; that boundary is where the zeta function's story begins.
why: Convergence questions decide where Dirichlet series define functions at all.

title: Asymptotic notation
summary: $f = O(g)$ and $f \ll g$ mean $|f| \le Cg$ for some constant; $f \sim g$ means $f/g \to 1$; $f = o(g)$ means $f/g \to 0$. Number theory statements are mostly sharp asymptotics with error terms.
why: Reading and comparing error terms is most of the skill in analytic number theory.
references: Apostol, Introduction to Analytic Number Theory
Montgomery & Vaughan, Multiplicative Number Theory I

title: Abel summation and Euler–Maclaurin
summary: Abel summation converts a sum $\sum a_n f(n)$ into an integral against the partial sums $A(t)=\sum_{n\le t} a_n$. Euler–Maclaurin compares $\sum f(n)$ with $\int f$ and gives constants such as Euler's $\gamma$.
key_statements: \sum_{n \le x} a_n f(n) = A(x) f(x) - \int_1^x A(t)\, f'(t)\, dt
why: It moves information between counting primes and weighting them by $\log p$.
references: Apostol, Introduction to Analytic Number Theory

title: Complex numbers and functions
summary: $e^{i\theta} = \cos\theta + i\sin\theta$; multiplication rotates and scales the plane. The variable of the zeta function is complex, $s = \sigma + it$, and its real part $\sigma$ is what the main conjectures are about.
why: Writing $n^{-s} = n^{-\sigma} e^{-it\log n}$ turns arithmetic into oscillation.

title: Holomorphic functions and Cauchy's theorem
summary: A complex-differentiable function on a domain has zero integral around closed loops, and Cauchy's integral formula recovers its values and all derivatives from boundary values. Holomorphic functions are locally power series.
why: Rigidity of holomorphic functions is why the zeta function's values on a line control it everywhere.

timeline.title: Cauchy's integral theorem
timeline.text: Founded complex contour integration, followed by the calculus of residues.

title: Residues and the argument principle
summary: A contour integral equals $2\pi i$ times the sum of residues inside. The argument principle and Rouché's theorem count zeros inside a contour, which is how zeros of $\zeta$ are counted.
why: Perron's formula and the explicit formula are residue computations.

leads_to.title: The Mellin transform and Perron's formula
Nontrivial zeros and the Riemann–von Mangoldt formula

timeline.title: Cauchy's integral theorem
timeline.text: Founded complex contour integration, followed by the calculus of residues.

title: Analytic continuation
summary: A holomorphic function is determined on a connected domain by its values on any small disc. $\sum z^n$ converges only for $|z|<1$, but its sum $1/(1-z)$ continues to all $z \ne 1$.
why: Values like $\zeta(-1) = -\tfrac1{12}$ come from continuation, not from summing the series.

timeline.title: On the Number of Primes Less Than a Given Magnitude
timeline.text: Continued $\zeta$ to the complex plane, proved the functional equation, linked zeros to primes and stated the Riemann hypothesis.
